item.text: `rg` is not installed in this container, so I’m falling back to the tiny file set here. There’s just `starter.hip`, which is pleasantly focused.

I’ve got the contract now. I’m going to make the kernel self-contained: one 32-value quantization group maps to a 32-thread tile, several tiles per block, so the memory layout stays simple and every scale/output byte is written exactly once.

I’m going to use wave-level shuffles with 32-lane subgroups. That matches the group size exactly, keeps the kernel light on LDS, and still gives deterministic tie handling through explicit threshold comparisons.
The first implementation is in place. I’m going to do a syntax compile if the HIP toolchain is present, and I’ll also give the bit-level rules another pass because the tiny edge cases here matter.

The code is compact enough to audit in one sweep. Next I’m compiling for `gfx950`; if the local HIP install doesn’t know that target I’ll still check the source with whatever target support is available.

The `gfx950` compile passed cleanly. I spotted one worthwhile performance cleanup before calling it done: the first version computed row/group offsets in every lane; I’m moving that to lane 0 per 32-value group and broadcasting the bases.
That cleanup is applied. I’m recompiling now, then I’ll do a small independent reference check of the rounding/scale logic on the CPU side to catch any threshold mistakes.

The second compile also passed. The remaining review is all about semantics now: signed zero uses the raw sign bit, scales use the exact requested exponent byte, and the tie thresholds alternate `<=`/`<` to pick the even nibble code.
Everything important is now in `starter.hip`; I’m doing one final diff check so I can report exactly what changed and avoid missing any accidental edits.
